summary:
Bill Elliott is a former NASCAR driver best known for winning the 1988 Winston Cup championship and the first Winston Million bonus in 1985. Born in Dawsonville, Georgia, in 1955, he began racing in NASCAR’s top series in 1976 and earned his first win in 1983.

Elliott won 44 Winston Cup races, including two Daytona 500s and three Southern 500s. His 1985 season included 11 wins and the million-dollar bonus for winning three major races. In 1987, he set qualifying-speed records at Daytona and Talladega that remain unsurpassed after restrictor plates were introduced at those tracks.

He won NASCAR’s Most Popular Driver Award a record 16 times. Named one of NASCAR’s 50 Greatest Drivers in 1998, Elliott entered the NASCAR Hall of Fame in 2015. His son Chase won the NASCAR Cup Series championship in 2020.
